javax.microedition.theme
Interface Element

All Known Subinterfaces:
ColorElement, ElementGroup, FontElement, MediaElement
public interface Element

Represents a customizable element in an appearance. Application developers use customizable elements by retrieving one or more of them from an appearance to query their contents. The information can be used in painting custom components, or by modifying the content of some element to cause appearance changes in the system if the implementation supports modify operations.

Each customizable element has an associated kind that indicates the type of the element's content, or tags it as an element group. Each element kind has a constant identifier defined in this interface.

In the case of a group, the feature and role of the group determine the meaning of the entire group, and the roles of the individual elements are interpreted in the context of the group. The features of the individual elements must be the same as the feature of the parent group. For example, a list item highlight is often made up of nine individual bitmaps, so a suitable customizable element structure would be a group containing nine elements with kind=Element.GRAPHIC. The File Format Reference section issues a recommendation about implementing and accessing such a group.

The content of the customizable element can be obtained with the getContent method. The following table collects the content types of elements and the corresponding result types of the getContent query.

getPresentation

java.util.Hashtable getPresentation()

Gets the presentation hints for this element, corresponding to the presentation attribute of the element tag in the appearance descriptor.

The presentation hints are returned as an instance of java.lang.Hashtable, where the keys and values correspond to the items and the conditionally mandatory values as described in "File Format Reference". For example, if the value of the presentation attribute is opacity=75;fit=stretch;valign=middle;halign=center, the Hashtable instance has the four keys "opacity", "fit", "valign", "halign" and corresponding values "75", "stretch", "middle" and "center", respectively. Applications can obtain individual hints directly from the hashtable.

If the element has no presentation attribute, this method must return null. If the presentation attribute is empty, or there was an error in the attribute value syntax, this method must return a Hashtable instance with no elements.

Returns:
a Hashtable instance of item keys and values, or null if the element has no presentation attribute

toString

java.lang.String toString()

Constructs a string representation of this Element instance. The string representation is implementation dependent, but must include at least the class name, kind, feature and role, and should include the actual value and its MIME type whenever it is practical.

The following string representations are typical examples:

[MediaElement: kind=graphic, feature=list, role=itemHighlight, type=image/svg+xml]

[ColorElement: kind=color, feature=text, role=labelColor, value=#000000]

[Element: kind=string, feature=greeting, role=hello, value=Hello, world!}

The string representation is intended for diagnostic purposes only, not for obtaining information about the element programmatically.

Overrides:
toString in class java.lang.Object
Returns:
the string representation
